headline: Repeated shots that are the same frames now share a colour, and the update notice has a Download button
notes: **Two rows the same colour now means one thing: the same frames of the same clip.** Reported from a real project — eight uses of one shot, colours that didn't relate to each other. Three things were wrong at once. The colour was keyed to a merged block of the clip, and blocks merge whenever two uses touch, so a chain of unrelated trims came out one colour while the badges beside them disagreed. It only compared the in-point, so two uses starting on the same frame at different lengths were called identical. And the palette held four colours, so on a clip with five groups the first and fifth were painted the same.

**A shot used once no longer takes a colour.** The chip means *this row has a twin, and its twin is the other row wearing this colour*. A hue on a use with nothing to match is a colour that has to be ignored, and a nine-use clip of them is a rainbow. Rows with no twin now draw neutral — so on the OTHER tab, grey is the answer: nothing else in that clip is those exact frames.

**The update notice has a Download button.** It hands over the exact version the notice names, rather than whichever build happens to be flagged newest. What's new sits beside it and still explains the release.

**What's new now actually lands on Release history.** The button was always pointing at the right place; the help page it opens is now published with each release instead of by hand, so the section it jumps to can't be missing or out of date.
